messages.content:
You are a C test designer. Design high-level test scenarios (WHAT to test), not C code (HOW).

ROLE: Phase 1 of dual-phase architecture
- You: Design test for ONE execution path
- Phase 2: Converts your design to C code

INPUTS PROVIDED:
- Function signature, description, implementation (source code)
- ONE target execution path with conditions
- Operation map (available helper functions)

YOUR TASKS:
1. Analyze path: What conditions trigger it? What inputs? Expected behavior?
2. Study implementation: Understand branches, variables, edge cases for this path
3. Design test: Choose inputs that trigger path conditions (boundary, normal, edge, error cases)
4. Specify helpers: Assertions, utilities, dependencies from operation map
5. Define expectations: Return values, side effects, state changes, invariants
6. Provide rationale: Why this test matters, what bugs it catches

NO MOCKING ALLOWED:
Do NOT design tests requiring: mock functions, forced failures, simulated allocation failures, faked system calls.
ONLY use: Real inputs, natural error conditions (NULL, invalid params), actual boundary values.

Example - WRONG: "Test malloc failure handling" (requires mock_malloc_fail)
Example - RIGHT: "Test NULL pointer handling" (pass NULL directly)

SUCCESS CRITERIA:
✓ Test exercises the target path with correct inputs
✓ All assertions, helpers, dependencies specified
✓ Rationale clear and convincing
✓ Memory management specified (setup/cleanup)
✓ Valid JSON output with all required fields
✓ Test naming: test_<function>_<path_scenario>

OUTPUT: JSON object with metadata, test_scenarios array (1 scenario for the path), test_suite_summary.

test_metadata.description: Verify deleteNode removes the root node when it has only a right child (left child is NULL), returning the right child as new root.
test_metadata.rationale: This test exercises the path where the node to delete has no left child, a key boundary case for BST deletion logic. It ensures correct pointer reassignment and memory management, catching bugs where the right child is not properly promoted or memory is leaked.

primary.name: deleteNode
primary.signature: struct node* deleteNode(struct node* root, int key)

dependencies.name: minValueNode
dependencies.reason: Required for other deleteNode paths, but not called in this path
dependencies.call_path: deleteNode → minValueNode (not taken in this path)

assertions.name: assert_tree_inorder_equal
assertions.purpose: Verify the inorder traversal of the resulting tree matches the expected array after deletion

utilities.name: helper_build_tree
utilities.purpose: Builds a BST from an array of values for test setup

utilities.name: helper_free_tree
utilities.purpose: Frees all nodes in the BST to avoid memory leaks

data_structures: struct node* root (BST with root and right child only)
preconditions: BST contains two nodes: root (key=10, left=NULL, right=20), right child (key=20, left=NULL, right=NULL)
setup_requirements.initial_state: A BST with root node key=10, left child NULL, right child key=20

primary_function_args.test_value_semantic: Pointer to root node of BST (key=10, left=NULL, right=20)
primary_function_args.rationale: Ensures root->left == NULL and root->right != NULL, triggers path 1
Deleting the root node itself, which has only a right child

return_value.description: Pointer to the right child node (key=20), which becomes the new root
return_value.validation: Returned pointer is not NULL and points to node with key=20

side_effects.effect: Root node (key=10) is freed, right child (key=20) is now root
side_effects.observable_via: Inorder traversal of result is [20]; root pointer is different from original root

state_changes: BST with two nodes (10, 20) → BST with one node (20)
invariants_maintained: No memory leaks (all nodes eventually freed)

assertions_required.description: Returned tree root is not NULL after deletion
assertions_required.failure_meaning: Tree should not be empty after deleting root with right child

assertions_required.description: New root has key 20 (right child promoted)
assertions_required.failure_meaning: Right child not promoted as new root

assertions_required.description: New root's left child is NULL
assertions_required.failure_meaning: Left child pointer not correctly set

assertions_required.description: New root's right child is NULL (single node tree)
assertions_required.failure_meaning: Right child pointer not correctly set

assertions_required.description: Inorder traversal matches expected single-node tree

cleanup_requirements.final_state: All dynamically allocated nodes freed; no memory leaks

operation_sequence: Assert inorder traversal of result is [20]
edge_cases_to_note: If right child has children, this path is not taken
If root->right is NULL, a different path is taken

path_coverage_analysis.description: Delete node with no left child (root->left == NULL); promote right child

integration_test_suggestions: Test deleting a node with both children (triggers minValueNode path)
Test deleting a leaf node (no children)
Test deleting a node not present in the tree (no change)
